The graph shows a portion of the curve $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and the line $y=\frac{1}{2}.$ Which of the following generates the $x$-values of all of their points of intersection? Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}.$ 

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/00d540b1f6412e4af2617452fbf0c58750d01e844d89d0d92cfacc0cb3e45e32.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi .
$$
